_comment: Canonical machine-readable programme metadata. Written by hand, read by
scripts/programme_model.py and through it by every generator, validator and
figure that needs a wave name, a phase ordering or the baseline identity.
It exists because each of these facts previously had two or three homes.
Wave membership was hard-coded in expand_packages.py AND in fig_waves.py,
both stopping at WP-140, so the nineteen packages added at v1.2.0 and
v1.3.0 were invisible to both while 02_wave_and_dependency_map.md listed
their waves in prose. The figure rendered '141 work-package documents' at a
moment the repository held 160, and nothing could see the difference.
Per-package facts — which wave a package is in, which phase it belongs to,
whether it carries a selector — live in package_dependency_matrix.csv, one
row per package. This file holds only what is true of the programme rather
than of a package: what the waves and phases MEAN, and in what order.

note: Three different things in this repository have been called a version, and
naming the kind is the whole point of this object. The COMMISSIONING
BASELINE is what the seal covers. The PROGRAMME DOCUMENT FORMAT VERSION is
the template generation the plan documents are written to. AETHRION itself
has no product version and will not have one until something ships.
v1.3.1 is a patch baseline because it adds no scientific capability. It
makes the v1.3.0 architecture internally executable — which it was not,
because two pre-go-live packages depended on Day-2 packages and the
cutover packages bound two acceptance scenarios where they meant 118.

scheduling_phases.name: Bootstrap
scheduling_phases.meaning: Makes acceptance possible at all; nothing else can be accepted before it

scheduling_phases.name: Before go-live
scheduling_phases.meaning: Must be ACCEPTED before the cutover decision can be taken

scheduling_phases.name: Cutover
scheduling_phases.meaning: The production cutover and the go-live decision itself

scheduling_phases.name: Hypercare
scheduling_phases.meaning: The bounded window immediately after cutover, with its own exit criteria

scheduling_phases.name: Day-2 continuous
scheduling_phases.meaning: A recurring rhythm that exists only once the system is running

phase_invariant.rule: A package whose scheduling phase is BOOTSTRAP, PRE_GO_LIVE or CUTOVER may not depend, directly or transitively, on a package whose phase is POST_GO_LIVE_HYPERCARE or DAY2_CONTINUOUS.
why: A dependency graph can be perfectly acyclic and still be impossible to
execute. If something required before go-live depends on something that
only exists after go-live, the programme has no valid starting order and
the acyclicity check will never say so.
Both violations this rule was written for were real: WP-152 depended on
the Day-2 postmortem rhythm to define a failure taxonomy that the rhythm
should consume, and WP-155 depended on recurring verifier recalibration
for an initial qualification it needs before anything runs.

waves.name: Scientific intelligence
waves.focus: study mode, search graph, epistemic memory

why_tiny: A general query language would need its own tests, its own failure modes
and its own document. The only aggregate this plan actually has is 'every
scenario of a given acceptance phase', so that is the only thing the
grammar expresses. An unknown key or value is a hard error, never an
empty result — an aggregate that silently resolves to nothing is the
failure mode a selector was introduced to remove.

_comment: Which packages MUST carry an aggregate selector, and which set they must
resolve to. Declared here rather than inferred from which packages happen
to have a selector column filled in, because a check anchored on the thing
it checks can be switched off by deleting that thing.
The self-test found this directly: with V-SCEN-002 iterating over packages
that HAVE a selector, deleting WP-115's selector made the rule pass in
silence — restoring exactly the two-scenario enumeration it exists to
prevent. The rule now iterates over this list, so removing a selector is
a validation failure rather than a quiet regression.
WP-119 is deliberately absent. It is the cutover REHEARSAL, and a
rehearsal that must first pass the entire commissioning suite is not a
rehearsal — it is the suite. It consumes WP-115's dossier through an
ordinary hard dependency instead. 04_P0 asks for this to be decided
rather than inferred; this is the decision.
